blank:0.en: Master Qingwu unrolled a long scroll of pale silk and set it before me on the low stone table. Every other disciple's name was already brushed in silver ink — yet one space remained, a *blank* near the centre, shaped like a held breath. She handed me the brush without a word.
blank:0.cnHint: 师尊将卷轴展开，上面只剩一处____等待我填写。
blank:0.hook: The brush trembled in my hand, and the ink began to glow.
blank:0.line: 'Fill the *blank*, and the mountain will know your name.'

reading:0.en: Shen Wujiu led me to the inner hall, where shelves of glowing jade slips rose to the ceiling. 'Each slip is a *reading*,' he said softly, 'a word that once saved a life or opened a sky.' I touched the nearest one and felt warmth travel up my arm like sunlight through water.
reading:0.cnHint: 师兄带我进入内堂，向我介绍那些发光的玉简是修行的____。
reading:0.hook: One slip at the very top pulsed red, as if warning me away.
reading:0.line: 'Choose your first *reading* carefully — some words choose back.'

list:0.en: Master Qingwu posted a *list* on the hall pillar each morning — ten words, ten powers, ten duties for the day. I read mine and felt each word settle in my chest like a stone into still water. Nine of the ten glowed softly. The tenth did not light at all.
list:0.cnHint: 师尊每天早晨在柱子上张贴一份____，规定当日须掌握的法术之词。
list:0.hook: The unlit word was the one that meant 'boundary.'
list:0.line: 'Study every word on the *list* before the evening bell.'

item:0.en: Shen Wujiu opened his travel chest and took out a single jade vial, turning it in the pale light. 'Each *item* a senior disciple carries has passed three trials,' he told me. 'This one holds the word for calm. Breathe it in only when the clouds below begin to spin.' He placed it in my palm.
item:0.cnHint: 师兄从行囊中取出一件____，叮嘱我只在危急时刻使用。
item:0.hook: The vial was cold, yet my hand began to sweat.
item:0.line: 'This *item* once kept a disciple from falling through the clouds.'

select:0.en: Before the morning lesson, Master Qingwu asked each of us to *select* one word from the hundred written on the wall. Most disciples reached for the bright ones — fly, heal, shield. I stood still, drawn instead to a small, dim word near the floor that none of the others seemed to see.
select:0.cnHint: 师尊要求每位弟子____一个字符作为今日修炼的根基。
select:0.hook: The dim word flickered once, as if it had been waiting for exactly me.
select:0.line: '*Select* with your instinct, not with your eyes.'

need:0.en: Xiaoxing found me at the edge of the outer terrace, staring down at the sea of clouds far below. She sat beside me quietly, then said I would *need* the word for anchor before I tried to fly. She pressed a small warm stone into my hand — the character for anchor carved deep into its face.
need:0.cnHint: 师妹告诉我，在尝试飞行之前____先掌握那个代表"锚"的法术字。
need:0.hook: Below us, a gap opened in the clouds, and something dark rose through it.
need:0.line: 'You *need* this word tonight — trust me on that.'

letter:0.en: The hall smelled of old wood and mountain wind. Master Qingwu placed a scroll before me, and I saw that each *letter* carved into its surface gave off a faint green glow, as if the word itself were alive. 'Read one aloud,' she said quietly, 'and the mountain will know your voice.' My fingers trembled above the first character.
letter:0.cnHint: 师尊将刻有发光____的卷轴放在我面前，要我开口诵读。
letter:0.hook: The last disciple who read aloud had not been seen since.
letter:0.line: 'Each *letter* on this scroll holds the breath of a living herb.'

sheet:0.en: Shen Wujiu handed me a single *sheet* of pale cloud-paper, still warm from the press. On it was my first formula — seven words arranged like stars. 'Copy it until your hand stops shaking,' he said, not unkindly. Outside the window, the sea of clouds below turned a deep, slow orange.
sheet:0.cnHint: 师兄递给我一____云纸，上面写着我的第一个法诀。
sheet:0.hook: A dark shape moved beneath the clouds, too large to be a bird.
sheet:0.line: 'This *sheet* carries the sect's oldest healing word — do not fold it.'

corresponding:0.en: Master Qingwu drew nine circles on the stone floor, each one paired with a word from the ancient list. 'Every herb has a *corresponding* sound,' she told us. 'Strike the wrong one and the plant will wither in your hand.' Xiaoxing nodded beside me, but her knuckle had already gone white around her brush.
corresponding:0.cnHint: 师尊解释说，每种灵草都有____的音声，用错便会枯萎。
corresponding:0.hook: One circle on the floor had already begun to crack.
corresponding:0.line: 'Find the *corresponding* word before the incense stick burns out.'

choose:0.en: Three scrolls lay open on the cedar table: one promised speed, one promised strength, one promised silence. Master Qingwu folded her hands and said nothing. I had to *choose* before the hall's lone candle finished its slow, steady burn. The smoke curled upward and took the shape of something I could not name.
choose:0.cnHint: 我必须在蜡烛燃尽前从三卷法诀中____一卷修习。
choose:0.hook: The candle flame bent sideways, though there was no wind.
choose:0.line: 'You must *choose* now — the mountain does not wait for doubt.'

single:0.en: Of the forty words on the board, Master Qingwu said only one truly mattered for tonight's test. I searched each line, heart loud in my ears, until I found it — a *single* character set apart by a thin circle of silver ink, humming at a pitch only I seemed to hear. The other disciples had not noticed it at all.
single:0.cnHint: 黑板上四十个字中，只有____一个字被银墨圈出，嗡嗡作响。
single:0.hook: When I touched the circle, the silver ink disappeared.
single:0.line: 'There is not a *single* mistake allowed when you speak a healing word.'

line:0.en: Xiaoxing pressed her brush to the cloud-paper and drew the first *line* of the word for 'wind.' It was thin and curved, no longer than my smallest finger, yet the air in the room shifted at once — scrolls rustled, sleeves lifted, and Master Qingwu's candle flame leaned hard to the left as if bowing.
line:0.cnHint: 师妹用毛笔写下'风'字的第一____，室内空气随即涌动。
line:0.hook: Beyond the shuttered window, the wind answered back with a sound like a name.
line:0.line: 'Every *line* of a word is a promise — write it as if you mean it.'

become:0.en: Shen Wujiu told me that words do not simply carry meaning in the Cloud Sea Sect — they *become* the thing they name the moment a trained voice speaks them. A word for rain, spoken in full, would wet the speaker's sleeve. I looked down at my palm, still dry, and wondered how long before mine could do the same.
become:0.cnHint: 师兄告诉我，受过训练的嗓音说出一个字，那个字就会____它所命名之物。
become:0.hook: Outside, a single drop of rain fell on a cloudless afternoon.
become:0.line: 'One day your words will *become* real wind and real fire — keep practicing.'

centre:0.en: The inner hall held a stone basin at its *centre*, filled with still water that reflected the floating peaks above. Master Qingwu said every disciple must stand here and speak their name into the water before training begins. I stepped forward and leaned over the basin. The reflection that looked back at me mouthed something different.
centre:0.cnHint: 内堂____有一只石盆，每位弟子须俯身对水说出自己的名字。
centre:0.hook: The water did not ripple — but the reflection slowly smiled.
centre:0.line: 'Stand at the *centre* and let the basin decide if your voice is true.'

letter:1.en: Master Qingwu unrolled a scroll on the stone table. Each *letter* carved into it glowed faintly, the way a firefly glows before a storm. 'Copy every one,' she said. 'A disciple who cannot read the words cannot hear the mountain.' I pressed my brush to silk and began.
letter:1.cnHint: 师尊展开刻有发光____的卷轴，命我逐一临摹。
letter:1.hook: But the last letter had no copy — it had already begun to copy me.
letter:1.line: 'Every *letter* on this scroll holds a breath of the mountain — copy it without fear.'

sheet:1.en: Shen Wujiu handed me a single *sheet* of pale cloud-silk, still warm from the drying rack above the cliff edge. 'One sheet, one chance,' he said quietly. I smoothed it flat and felt the mountain breathe through my fingertips. The wind held still, waiting.
sheet:1.cnHint: 师兄递给我一张云丝____，说只有一次机会。
sheet:1.hook: Then a second sheet fell from nowhere and landed face-down at my feet.
sheet:1.line: 'Guard this *sheet* well — cloud-silk torn by doubt will never mend.'

corresponding:1.en: Master Qingwu drew twelve root-words on the board and beside each one left a blank. 'Find the *corresponding* herb in the garden below,' she said, 'and the formula will open for you.' I matched nine before the mist thickened. Three herbs remained hidden. Three blanks stared back.
corresponding:1.cnHint: 师尊让我在花园中找到与根词____的灵草，配成药方。
corresponding:1.hook: The tenth herb had moved since dawn — and something had moved it.
corresponding:1.line: 'Each root-word has a *corresponding* herb; miss one and the formula breaks.'

choose:1.en: At the gate of the Cloud Sea Sect stood three paths: stone steps, a rope bridge, and a narrow ledge above open sky. Shen Wujiu crossed his arms. 'New disciples must *choose* alone,' he said. I studied each path. The ledge hummed softly, like a word about to be spoken.
choose:1.cnHint: 三条路摆在面前，师兄说新弟子必须独自____。
choose:1.hook: Whichever path I left behind, something on it exhaled with relief.
choose:1.line: 'You must *choose* your own path — the mountain will not choose for you.'

single:1.en: The garden of spiritual herbs held hundreds of plants, yet Master Qingwu pointed to one small corner. 'Not a *single* word-herb here has bloomed this season,' she said, her voice measured and still. I knelt beside the soil. The roots were intact, the leaves healthy — but the flowers were missing. Only their shadows remained.
single:1.cnHint: 师尊指着灵草园的一角，说今季没有____一株开花。
single:1.hook: Then one shadow stretched toward me, slow as a held breath.
single:1.line: 'Not a *single* herb blooms here — tell me what you sense in the soil.'

line:1.en: Xiaoxing showed me the first formula: seven words arranged in a straight *line* across the training stone, each one linked to the next like beads on a cord. 'Break the line and the spell collapses,' she warned, her eyes bright. I read the words aloud. A thin seam of light ran along the stone and held.
line:1.cnHint: 师妹展示了七个字排成一____的咒文，告诫我不可断开。
line:1.hook: The light held — but the last word blinked once, like a closing eye.
line:1.line: 'Read every word in the *line* in order, or the mountain will not listen.'

become:1.en: 'Words do not stay words,' Master Qingwu said, watching me struggle with the healing formula. 'Spoken with full breath, they *become* medicine; spoken in fear, they become noise.' I tried again. The herb in my palm warmed slightly. It was not medicine yet, but it was no longer just a word.
become:1.cnHint: 师尊说，字句以完整的气息吐出，就会____药；否则只是噪音。
become:1.hook: Outside, the clouds below the mountain began to rise without cause.
become:1.line: 'Let the words *become* what they must — your breath is the only key.'

centre:1.en: Shen Wujiu led me to the training court and pointed to a flat stone at its exact *centre*. 'Stand there and speak your name,' he said. I walked to the stone. The mountain seemed to lean in. I spoke. A ring of faint mist spread outward from my feet and faded at the court's edge.
centre:1.cnHint: 师兄带我站在练功场正____的石头上，让我说出自己的名字。
centre:1.hook: But the mist did not fade completely — one thin thread curled back toward the stone.
centre:1.line: 'The stone at the *centre* of this court remembers every name ever spoken on it.'

passage:1.en: The stone gate of the Cloud Sea Sect stood at the mountain edge, its arch carved with ancient symbols. I stepped through the narrow *passage* between two moss-covered pillars, feeling the air shift — cool and charged, as if the mountain itself was drawing breath. Shen Wujiu waited on the other side, his robe still. 'Welcome,' he said quietly.
passage:1.cnHint: 我穿过两根石柱之间的____，感受到山门内外空气截然不同。
passage:1.hook: Behind me, the gate sealed shut without a sound.
passage:1.line: 'Every disciple must walk this *passage* alone — the mountain decides if you may stay.'

base:1.en: Shen Wujiu led me to the great stone pillar at the sect's entrance. 'Read the words carved at the *base*,' he said. I knelt and traced the deep letters with one finger. They hummed beneath my touch, warm as sunlight. Each word was a seed of power, waiting for someone who understood it to make it bloom.
base:1.cnHint: 师兄让我读刻在石柱____的文字，那些字在我指尖震动。
base:1.hook: The last word at the bottom had no translation — only a shape like a rising wave.
base:1.line: 'The rules of our sect are carved at the *base* — read them before you climb any higher.'

section:1.en: Master Qingwu handed me a worn scroll. 'Begin with the third *section*,' she said. I unrolled it carefully. The words there were simpler, but each one glowed faintly, like a candle behind thin paper. Xiaoxing leaned close and whispered, 'Those words can calm a storm if you say them right.'
section:1.cnHint: 青雾师尊让我从卷轴的第三个____开始学习，那里的字发着微光。
section:1.hook: At the scroll's edge, one word had been crossed out in red.
section:1.line: 'Do not skip ahead — the third *section* holds what you need most right now.'

answer:1.en: At the mountain gate, an old stone tablet posed a riddle in carved letters. Every new disciple had to give an *answer* before entering. I stood before it, heart steady, and spoke one word — the name of the wind that lifts clouds. The tablet cracked softly down the middle, and the path beyond lit up.
answer:1.cnHint: 入山门前，每位弟子必须给出石碑上谜题的____。
answer:1.hook: From deep inside the crack, something began to glow green.
answer:1.line: 'Your *answer* was correct — but the tablet remembers every wrong one too.'

study:1.en: Xiaoxing found me sitting outside the gate with an open scroll across my knees. 'You started your *study* before the ceremony?' she asked, eyes wide. I nodded. The morning mist carried the scent of pine and something sharper — like ink on stone. She sat beside me without another word and opened her own scroll.
study:1.cnHint: 小星发现我在仪式开始之前就已经独自开始____了。
study:1.hook: A single cloud drifted below the mountain, shaped exactly like an open book.
study:1.line: 'Your *study* begins the moment you arrive — the mountain has already been watching.'

mark:1.en: Before I crossed the gate, Master Qingwu pressed her thumb to my forehead. A faint *mark* appeared there, shaped like a small flame. 'All Cloud Sea disciples carry this,' Shen Wujiu explained. 'The mountain reads it.' I touched the spot gently. The skin was warm, and the flame seemed to flicker when I breathed.
mark:1.cnHint: 入门前，青雾师尊在我额头留下一个____，形如小小的火焰。
mark:1.hook: That night, a second flame appeared on the stone wall beside my bed.
mark:1.line: 'Guard your *mark* well — it shows where your words have reached so far.'

choice:1.en: Two paths wound away from the sect gate. The left led up through white mist toward the inner peaks; the right curved down to the practice fields below. Master Qingwu said nothing — she only watched. I understood that this *choice* was the first lesson. I breathed once, then took the upward path.
choice:1.cnHint: 山门内两条路分开，师尊沉默地看着，这个____本身就是第一堂课。
choice:1.hook: As I climbed, the lower path quietly disappeared behind the mist.
choice:1.line: 'Every disciple faces this *choice* — the mountain learns your nature from it.'

part:1.en: Shen Wujiu walked me through the outer yard of the sect and pointed to each building in turn. 'This *part* of the mountain belongs to the first-year disciples,' he said, sweeping his hand across the lower terraces. The rooftops were pale wood, still new. High above, older structures rose like dark birds into the cloud.
part:1.cnHint: 师兄向我介绍山上属于新弟子的这个____，更高处的建筑隐入云中。
part:1.hook: One high rooftop had a light burning in it that no one had lit.
part:1.line: 'Learn this *part* well before you ask to see what lies above the cloud line.'

bank:0.en: The inner hall held a great *bank* of wooden drawers, each carved with a single word glowing faintly gold. Master Qingwu said every drawer stored one formula, and together they formed the living memory of the Cloud Sea Sect. I counted the rows and felt very small. Somewhere in those drawers, my own name waited to be written.
bank:0.cnHint: 师尊向我展示藏有无数法诀的____，每个抽屉里都封存着一个发光的字。
bank:0.hook: One drawer, I noticed, had no glow at all.
bank:0.line: 'This *bank* of words holds every secret our sect has ever learned,' said Master Qingwu.

statement:0.en: Before the stone altar, each new disciple had to speak a *statement* of intention — one clear sentence naming the word they most wished to master. When my turn came, the hall fell silent. I chose the word 'rise.' The candle flames all leaned toward me at once, as if listening.
statement:0.cnHint: 每位新弟子必须在石坛前说出一句____，表明自己最想领悟的那个字。
statement:0.hook: The flames did not lean toward anyone else.
statement:0.line: 'Your *statement* must be honest,' said Shen Wujiu, 'the altar always knows.'

identify:0.en: Master Qingwu spread twelve scrolls across the floor and asked me to *identify* the one that hummed. I pressed my palm above each in turn, feeling nothing, then nothing, then a faint warmth like morning sun. I named the seventh scroll. She nodded slowly, eyes unreadable.
identify:0.cnHint: 师尊让我在十二卷书轴中____出那卷会轻声鸣响的，以此测试我的感知力。
identify:0.hook: The seventh scroll had no words written on it at all.
identify:0.line: 'Can you *identify* which word in this room is dying?' Master Qingwu asked softly.

comprehension:0.en: Shen Wujiu handed me a thin jade slip and said *comprehension* of its single carved word would take most disciples a full season. I held it to the lamplight, breathed slowly, and felt the meaning open like a flower — in moments, not months. His smile was warm but brief.
comprehension:0.cnHint: 师兄告诉我，真正的____不是背诵，而是让刻在玉简上的字在心中自然绽放。
comprehension:0.hook: Outside, a cloud shaped like an open eye drifted past the window.
comprehension:0.line: 'Real *comprehension* is not speed,' Shen Wujiu said, 'but I have never seen it this fast.'

require:0.en: The first lesson was strict: the highest healing words *require* a calm heart above all else. Master Qingwu made me hold a small flame in my cupped hands — not a real flame, but a word-flame, cold and fragile. It steadied only when my breathing did. Then she blew it out.
require:0.cnHint: 师尊教导我，最强的治愈之字____修行者拥有平静如水的内心，否则那字会自行熄灭。
require:0.hook: She said she would not light it for me a second time.
require:0.line: 'These words *require* more patience than you have shown so far,' said Master Qingwu.

least:0.en: Of all the disciples who entered the hall that morning, I owned the *least* — no jade pendant, no family formula, only a worn cloth bag and a single word my grandmother once whispered to me. Master Qingwu looked at my empty hands the longest before she finally smiled.
least:0.cnHint: 在所有新弟子中，我带来的东西____，却是师尊注视时间最长的那一个。
least:0.hook: That whispered word from my grandmother glowed faintly through the cloth bag.
least:0.line: 'Those with the *least* at the gate,' said Master Qingwu, 'often carry the most inside.'

following:0.en: Master Qingwu read aloud the *following* three rules of the inner library: never copy a word without permission, never speak a formula above your rank, never enter alone after dark. Her voice was even and soft. Yet the wall behind her cast four shadows, though only three of us stood there.
following:0.cnHint: 师尊宣读了内藏室的规矩，在场弟子都在认真听她说的____几条戒律。
following:0.hook: No one mentioned the fourth shadow, and no one looked away from it.
following:0.line: 'Remember the *following* rule above all others,' said Master Qingwu, 'silence protects the word.'

decide:0.en: At the end of the first day, Xiaoxing pulled me aside and said every disciple must *decide* one thing before sleeping: which word would they sacrifice if they could only keep one. I had not known this was required. I lay awake all night, and by dawn, I still had no answer.
decide:0.cnHint: 小星悄悄告诉我，每位弟子在入门第一夜都必须____自己愿意舍弃哪个字。
decide:0.hook: At first light, a single feather — black and rimmed with silver — landed on my windowsill.
decide:0.line: 'You must *decide* before the candle dies,' Xiaoxing whispered, 'or the word decides for you.'

passage:0.en: Master Qingwu led me through a narrow *passage* carved into the living rock of the mountain. Glowing characters lined both walls, breathing softly in the dark like sleeping things. 'Each word you read here feeds your spirit root,' she said. I reached out and touched one — and felt it reach back.
passage:0.cnHint: 师尊带我穿过山腹中的一条____，两壁刻满发光的灵字。
passage:0.hook: Behind me, the carved door sealed shut without a sound.
passage:0.line: 'This *passage* holds every word our sect has ever lost and found.'

base:0.en: The great library tower rose from a wide stone platform, and Shen Wujiu showed me the carvings at its *base*. 'These are the first words ever spoken on the Cloud Sea,' he said quietly. Moss had grown over two of them. I knelt and brushed it away, and the stone beneath my fingers grew warm.
base:0.cnHint: 师兄指着藏书塔____处的古老铭文，说那是云海派最初的灵字。
base:0.hook: The warmth spread up my arm and did not stop.
base:0.line: 'Read the words at the *base* before you dare to read the ones above.'

section:0.en: The library was divided by silk curtains, and only the outer *section* was open to new disciples. Xiaoxing counted the curtains with me — nine in all, each one a deeper shade of blue. 'I have only ever passed the third,' she whispered. On the ceiling above the ninth curtain, something moved.
section:0.cnHint: 藏书阁被分成若干____，新弟子只能进入最外侧的区域。
section:0.hook: A shape pressed against the ninth curtain from the other side.
section:0.line: 'Stay in this *section* — the inner words are not yet yours to hold.'

answer:0.en: Master Qingwu placed an open scroll before me and asked what the central character meant. I stared until my eyes ached. No *answer* came from my mind — but one rose from somewhere lower, somewhere I had not known existed. I spoke it aloud without understanding how. The candle flames in the room all bent toward me.
answer:0.cnHint: 师尊要我解读卷轴上的灵字，我的____并非来自头脑，而是来自更深处。
answer:0.hook: Master Qingwu folded the scroll and said nothing at all.
answer:0.line: 'The right *answer* will not always feel like thinking — sometimes it feels like remembering.'

study:0.en: My *study* of the first-level texts was meant to take a full season. By the third morning I had finished them, and the room felt too small. Shen Wujiu found me sitting on the windowsill above the cloud sea, the last scroll already rolled shut in my lap. He looked at me the way one looks at an unexpected storm.
study:0.cnHint: 我对初阶灵文的____进展太快，师兄看我的眼神像在看一场意外的风暴。
study:0.hook: He took the scroll from my lap and checked it twice.
study:0.line: 'Quick *study* is a gift — but gifts with no root tend to wither fast.'

mark:0.en: Shen Wujiu inked a small *mark* on the inside of my wrist before my first test — a character for 'steady,' he said, to quiet nerves. I entered the examining room and the character burned cold for just a moment, then settled. I passed. But when I looked at my wrist afterward, the ink had changed shape.
mark:0.cnHint: 师兄在我手腕内侧留下一个____，帮我在考核时稳定心神，但考后那个字变形了。
mark:0.hook: The new shape was not a word I had ever been taught.
mark:0.line: 'Every disciple earns their first *mark* — what matters is which one chooses you back.'

choice:0.en: Two scrolls lay on the table: one red, one grey. Master Qingwu told me the *choice* was mine alone — the red scroll taught words of force, the grey taught words of mending. I held each one. The grey was heavier than it looked. I set the red scroll down and did not regret it, until I heard what was coming up the mountain path.
choice:0.cnHint: 师尊让我在两卷灵文之间自行____，我选了治愈之道，直到听见山路上的动静。
choice:0.hook: Footsteps — too many, and moving too fast.
choice:0.line: 'A *choice* made in peace will be tested in haste — that is how the sect knows it was real.'

part:0.en: Xiaoxing told me that memorising words was only one *part* of cultivation — the smaller part, she insisted, tapping her own chest. The larger part lived in the breath and the bone, she said, and could not be read from any page. She demonstrated by speaking a single word that made the ink in my open scroll rise and float. I had memorised that same word an hour ago and felt nothing.
part:0.cnHint: 师妹告诉我，记忆灵字只是修炼的一个____，更大的那部分藏在呼吸与骨骼里。
part:0.hook: She closed my scroll and said, 'Now forget everything you read.'
part:0.line: 'Memory is only one *part* — the word must also trust the voice that carries it.'

bank:1.en: Master Qingwu led us to the edge of the floating mountain, where the great *bank* of ancient words was carved into the stone cliff. Each character glowed faintly, holding centuries of gathered spiritual meaning. 'Study these,' she said, 'before the clouds rise.' I pressed my hand to the cold rock and felt the words breathe.
bank:1.cnHint: 清雾师尊带我们来到石壁前，那里存放着古老词汇的____。
bank:1.hook: One character near the bottom had begun to fade.
bank:1.line: 'This *bank* of words holds every healing formula the sect has ever known.'

statement:1.en: At the gate of the Cloud Sea Sect, a senior disciple read aloud a single *statement* carved on a white stone tablet. It named each virtue a true disciple must carry: clarity, patience, and an open mind. The morning mist swallowed his last word before it could reach my ears fully.
statement:1.cnHint: 在门派入口，师兄朗读了石碑上的一段____，列出弟子应有的品德。
statement:1.hook: The stone tablet cracked down the middle without a sound.
statement:1.line: Shen Wujiu said, '*Statement* made — now we see if your actions match it.'

identify:1.en: Xiaoxing handed me a bundle of dried spiritual herbs and asked me to *identify* each one by scent alone. I closed my eyes. The sharp bite of wind-root, the sweet hush of cloud-blossom — I named them slowly, one by one. On the last herb I hesitated, and she went very still.
identify:1.cnHint: 师妹让我仅凭气味来____每一株灵草。
identify:1.hook: The final herb had no scent at all.
identify:1.line: 'Can you *identify* this one? No disciple has managed it in three years.'

comprehension:1.en: Master Qingwu placed a single line of script before me and waited. My *comprehension* of the old characters was weak, and the meaning slipped like water through my fingers. She did not rush me. Outside, the clouds shifted, and a cold wind moved through the hall without opening any door.
comprehension:1.cnHint: 面对古老文字，我的____十分有限，师尊静静等候。
comprehension:1.hook: The script began to rearrange itself while I watched.
comprehension:1.line: 'Your *comprehension* will grow — but only if you stop trying to force it.'

require:1.en: The entrance trial did not *require* great strength or speed. It asked only that I hold a single word in my mind and speak it aloud with steady breath. Shen Wujiu watched from the arch above, arms folded. I breathed in, breathed out, and spoke. The mountain hummed beneath my feet.
require:1.cnHint: 入门考验并不____力量，只需平静地念出一个字。
require:1.hook: The hum beneath my feet grew louder after I spoke.
require:1.line: 'The sect does not *require* perfection — it requires honesty.'

least:1.en: Of all the new disciples gathered at the outer gate, I had studied for the *least* number of years. The others carried worn scrolls and spoke the old words easily. I carried nothing but a quiet wish. Xiaoxing smiled at me from across the courtyard, as if that were already enough.
least:1.cnHint: 所有新弟子中，我学习的年限____，但师妹的微笑给了我力量。
least:1.hook: A single white crane landed on my empty hands.
least:1.line: 'At *least* you came without fear — that is rarer than you think.'

following:1.en: The *following* morning brought thick mist and a message from Master Qingwu pinned to our door. It listed three tasks, each harder than the last: collect dew from the highest peak, copy one hundred characters before noon, and sit in silence until the clouds parted. Shen Wujiu read it twice, then smiled grimly.
following:1.cnHint: ____天清晨，师尊留下字条，列出了三项越来越难的任务。
following:1.hook: The clouds showed no sign of parting by nightfall.
following:1.line: 'The *following* tasks will test what you are made of — rest while you can.'

decide:1.en: At the fork in the mountain path, I had to *decide* alone: the left trail led to the herb gardens, the right to the copy hall where Master Qingwu waited. Both mattered. Both were urgent. The wind pushed equally from both sides, offering no guidance. A single feather drifted down from above.
decide:1.cnHint: 站在山路分叉处，我必须独自____走哪条路。
decide:1.hook: The feather stopped in mid-air and did not fall.
decide:1.line: 'You must *decide* for yourself — the path does not choose its walker.'

blank:1.en: The stone gate of Cloud Sea Sect rose before me like a frozen wave. An elder pressed a cold jade tablet into my hands. Every disciple's name was carved into it — but where mine should have been, there was only a *blank*, smooth and silent as the clouds below. 'Fill it yourself,' the elder said, and walked away.
blank:1.cnHint: 弟子们的名字都刻在玉牌上，唯独我的位置是一片____。
blank:1.hook: The blank began to glow the moment I touched it.
blank:1.line: 'Your name goes in that *blank* — but only after you prove you have earned it.'

reading:1.en: Shen Wujiu handed me a thin scroll on the mountain path, its edges worn soft by a hundred hands. '*Reading* this before the gate opens is the oldest custom of the Sect,' he said quietly. 'The words feed your spirit the way morning mist feeds the stones.' I unrolled it. The characters shimmered.
reading:1.cnHint: 师兄说，进山门前____这卷古籍是门派最古老的习俗。
reading:1.hook: One line near the end had been scratched out — recently.
reading:1.line: '*Reading* it once is enough for most disciples — but you may need it twice.'

list:1.en: Master Qingwu stood at the peak and read aloud from a long paper scroll — the entrance *list* of new disciples. Name after name floated out over the clouds like seeds on wind. When she reached mine, she paused. The pause lasted three full breaths. Then she continued.
list:1.cnHint: 师尊宣读新弟子的____时，念到我的名字后停顿了一下。
list:1.hook: No one else seemed to notice the pause but Xiaoxing.
list:1.line: 'Every name on this *list* carries the weight of the mountain — do not forget that.'

item:1.en: Before crossing the gate, each disciple laid one personal *item* on the offering stone: a coin, a dried flower, a worn button. These small things formed a quiet line under the sky. I placed my father's old ink brush. The stone hummed beneath it for a moment, as if tasting the memory inside.
item:1.cnHint: 每位弟子要在迎客石上放下一件____，我放了父亲的旧毛笔。
item:1.hook: When I looked back, my brush was the only item still glowing.
item:1.line: 'Choose your *item* with care — the mountain remembers what you give it.'

select:1.en: At the gate, Xiaoxing whispered that Master Qingwu did not *select* disciples at random. Every name had been watched for a full year from afar, she said — our words, our silences, even the way we walked in rain. I thought of every careless thing I had ever said, and my chest tightened.
select:1.cnHint: 小星悄悄告诉我，师尊____弟子从来不是随机的，每个人都被暗中观察了整整一年。
select:1.hook: Then Xiaoxing added: 'She almost did not select you.'
select:1.line: 'Master Qingwu did not *select* us for our strength — she selected us for our doubt.'

need:1.en: The cloud bridge connecting the outer peak to the inner gate was narrower than my arm-span. Shen Wujiu crossed it without looking down. I stopped halfway. 'You do not *need* courage right now,' he called back, voice steady as carved stone. 'You only need one more step.' I took it.
need:1.cnHint: 站在云桥中央，师兄说我现在____的不是勇气，只是再迈一步。
need:1.hook: The bridge dissolved into mist the instant my foot left it.
need:1.line: 'You *need* to stop looking at the clouds below and start looking at the gate ahead.'

letter:2.en: Master Qingwu unrolled an ancient scroll and pointed to a single mark. 'This *letter*,' she said quietly, 'holds the breath of the wind.' I traced its shape with one finger, and the air around my hand began to stir. Outside, the cloud sea rippled without cause.
letter:2.cnHint: 青悟师尊展开古卷，指着其中一个____，说它藏着风的气息。
letter:2.hook: The clouds below the mountain began to spin in the shape of that very mark.
letter:2.line: 'Each *letter* on this scroll is a living breath — learn it with care.'

sheet:2.en: Shen Wujiu handed me a thin *sheet* of pale bark-paper, covered edge to edge in fine spirit-marks. 'Copy every symbol before dawn,' he said, and left without another word. The marks seemed to glow faintly as the night deepened around me.
sheet:2.cnHint: 师兄递给我一____薄薄的树皮纸，上面密密麻麻写满了灵文。
sheet:2.hook: By midnight, one symbol had vanished from the page entirely.
sheet:2.line: 'Guard this *sheet* well — it carries half the healing art of our sect.'

corresponding:2.en: Each spirit-herb in the stone garden had a *corresponding* word carved beside it on a small wooden sign. I matched herb to word and felt a soft warmth rise in my palm. Master Qingwu watched from the doorway, saying nothing, only nodding once.
corresponding:2.cnHint: 石园里每株灵草旁都刻着与它____的灵字，我一一配对，掌心生出暖意。
corresponding:2.hook: One sign stood alone — its herb was missing, and the soil around it was cold.
corresponding:2.line: 'Find the *corresponding* herb for each word, and the formula will open to you.'

choose:2.en: Three scrolls lay before me on the stone table: one the colour of morning mist, one of deep pine, one of amber cloud. 'You may *choose* only one to study this season,' Master Qingwu said. I reached out — then pulled my hand back, uncertain.
choose:2.cnHint: 三卷古籍摆在石桌上，师尊说我只能____其中一卷研习。
choose:2.hook: Whichever scroll I did not choose began to tremble on its own.
choose:2.line: '*Choose* with your breath, not your eyes — the right scroll will feel warm.'

single:2.en: Among a hundred spirit-marks painted on the cave wall, Xiaoxing pointed to one. 'This *single* word,' she whispered, 'once lifted an entire mountain.' I looked at its simple strokes and felt something stir deep in my chest, like a bell struck far away.
single:2.cnHint: 洞壁上百个灵字中，师妹指着____一个字，说它曾举起整座山。
single:2.hook: As we turned to leave, that one word on the wall began to shine gold.
single:2.line: 'A *single* true word outweighs a thousand empty ones — remember that.'

line:2.en: Master Qingwu drew one slow *line* in the air with her finger, and a faint silver trail hung there like smoke that refused to fade. 'Your spirit follows the path of the stroke,' she said. I tried — my line wobbled, thin and pale, but it held.
line:2.cnHint: 青悟师尊在空中缓缓画出一条____，银色的轨迹悬而不散。
line:2.hook: At the far end of my wavering line, a small cold light began to form.
line:2.line: 'Every *line* you draw in the air is a promise to the sky — make it true.'

become:2.en: Shen Wujiu sat beside me on the cliff edge and said, 'The word does not serve you. You must *become* the word — breathe its shape, carry its weight.' I closed my eyes and tried. For one short moment the wind stopped, as if listening.
become:2.cnHint: 师兄告诉我，修行者不是使用灵字，而是要____灵字本身。
become:2.hook: When I opened my eyes, my shadow on the rock had changed its outline.
become:2.line: 'To *become* the word is the first true step — everything before it is practice.'

centre:2.en: In the Hall of First Study, a single lamp hung at the *centre* of the ceiling, casting equal light to every corner. Xiaoxing told me that the flame never went out and never grew. I stood beneath it and felt, for the first time, completely still.
centre:2.cnHint: 初学堂正____悬着一盏长明灯，师妹说它从不熄灭，也从不变大。
centre:2.hook: Tonight the lamp flickered once — the first time in a hundred years, the elders said.
centre:2.line: 'Stand at the *centre* of the hall and let the light fall on you equally from all sides.'

blank:2.en: Inside the Hall of First Words, each new disciple receives a stone tablet. Mine arrived this morning — smooth, cool, and covered in faint lines waiting to be filled. One section near the bottom held a single *blank*, a space left open, as if the sect itself had saved a question only I could answer. I pressed my finger against it and felt a faint warmth rise.
blank:2.cnHint: 石碑上有一处____，似乎在等待弟子用自己的答案来填满它。
blank:2.hook: The warmth spread upward, and the lines began to glow.
blank:2.line: 'Leave no *blank* unfilled — the sect will know if you do,' Shen Wujiu said quietly.

reading:2.en: Master Qingwu set a slim jade scroll on the table before me. 'Your first task,' she said, and left without another word. I spent the whole afternoon in *reading*, turning each line over slowly, feeling the characters hum against my palms like bees trapped in warm stone. By dusk I had learned only three words — but those three words smelled of rain.
reading:2.cnHint: 师尊交给我一卷玉简，我用了整个下午做____，才从中感受到三个字的气息。
reading:2.hook: On the final page, someone had pressed a single dark fingerprint.
reading:2.line: '*Reading* this scroll once is not enough — let the words enter your breathing,' said Master Qingwu.

list:2.en: Xiaoxing slid a paper under my door before dawn. On it was a *list* of twelve herbs — each one a word in the Cloud Sea Sect's oldest healing formula. Beside each name she had drawn a tiny star or a small cross: stars meant the herb still grew on the mountain, crosses meant it had gone silent and must be searched for in the clouds below.
list:2.cnHint: 晓星把一份含有十二种灵草的____悄悄塞到我门下，还用星号和叉号标出了各自的状态。
list:2.hook: The last name on the list had neither star nor cross — only a smear of ash.
list:2.line: 'Keep this *list* close,' Xiaoxing whispered, 'and tell no one how many crosses you count.'

item:2.en: Among the objects left in my room by the previous disciple, one *item* stood apart from the rest: a small wooden box sealed with a cord of woven cloud-silk. The other things — a worn brush, two empty jars, a folded robe — felt ordinary. This one felt like a held breath. I set it on the highest shelf and did not open it.
item:2.cnHint: 前任弟子留下的东西里，有一件____显得格外不寻常，我选择把它放到最高处，没有打开。
item:2.hook: That night the box made a single soft sound, like a word being swallowed.
item:2.line: 'Every *item* left behind holds the last thought of the one who owned it,' Shen Wujiu told me.

select:2.en: Shen Wujiu led me to the Herb Wall, where hundreds of sealed jars lined the stone shelves from floor to ceiling. 'You may *select* one word-herb to study this month,' he said. I stood for a long time, looking. Some jars shivered. Some were perfectly still. I reached at last for a small green one near the corner — and the jar beside it fell.
select:2.cnHint: 师兄带我到灵草墙前，让我____一株本月研习的字草，我刚伸手，旁边的罐子却突然落下。
select:2.hook: The jar did not break — it hovered, spinning slowly, waiting.
select:2.line: '*Select* with your instinct, not your eyes,' Shen Wujiu said, watching my hand.

need:2.en: I found a note folded inside my sleeping mat: three lines in small, careful characters. The first said the morning bell had changed meaning. The second said to trust the smell of rain. The third said, 'You *need* the word for shelter before the next cloud-storm arrives.' I did not know who had written it. The ink was still faintly warm.
need:2.cnHint: 我在睡垫里发现一张字条，上面说在下次云暴来临前，我____学会'庇护'这个字。
need:2.hook: Outside, the clouds below the mountain were already turning the colour of iron.
need:2.line: 'You *need* that word tonight — not tomorrow, not at dawn,' the note seemed to insist.

passage:2.en: The gate to the inner hall was sealed by a carved stone door. Shen Wujiu pressed his palm to the wall beside it, and a narrow *passage* appeared — just wide enough for one person, lined with glowing moss that hummed like a held breath. 'Step through quickly,' he said. 'It closes at dawn.' Behind me, the stone door began to tremble.
passage:2.cnHint: 师兄带我发现了一条隐藏的____，穿过后石门便会关闭。
passage:2.hook: Something on the other side whispered back through the moss.
passage:2.line: 'This *passage* was carved by the first disciple, and only sect members may use it.'

base:2.en: I found the old stone pillar at the edge of the cliff, half hidden by cloud. Words were carved around its *base* — not in any script I knew, but each one seemed to press warmth into my fingers as I traced them. Master Qingwu had mentioned a pillar like this once, in a lesson I had almost slept through. The carvings pulsed once, faint and gold, then faded.
base:2.cnHint: 我在石柱的____处发现了神秘文字，轻触后它们竟然发光。
base:2.hook: The warmth climbed my arm and did not stop at my wrist.
base:2.line: 'Read from the *base* upward — the words grow stronger as they rise.'

section:2.en: The library scroll was longer than both my arms. Xiaoxing unrolled only one *section* — the middle part — and held it close to the lamp. 'Here,' she said softly. 'This is where the healing words begin.' The characters on that portion shimmered with a faint green light, as if the scroll itself breathed. Outside, wind moved through the bamboo in a pattern that sounded almost like speech.
section:2.cnHint: 小星只展开了书卷的某个____，那里的文字散发着绿光。
section:2.hook: The wind through the bamboo formed a word neither of us had taught ourselves.
section:2.line: 'Only this *section* of the scroll has ever been successfully read aloud.'

answer:2.en: I left my question on a slip of paper at the foot of Master Qingwu's door: why did the healing word I spoke this morning turn grey instead of green? No one came. At dusk, I found the slip returned under my own door. The *answer* written below my question was only three words long — but each word glowed a different colour, and together they formed a shape like a key. I did not yet know what lock it opened.
answer:2.cnHint: 我把问题纸条放在师尊门前，傍晚收到了只有三个词的____。
answer:2.hook: The three glowing words rearranged themselves while I watched.
answer:2.line: 'An *answer* given too early becomes a wall instead of a door.'

study:2.en: Shen Wujiu led me to a small room at the back of the east wing: his personal *study*. Scrolls covered every surface, and dried spirit-herbs hung from the beams, still faintly fragrant. 'You will practise here each evening,' he said, setting a blank scroll on the low table. 'Words learned alone fade. Words learned in this room seem to last.' One of the hanging herbs swayed, though the window was shut.
study:2.cnHint: 师兄带我进入他的____，说在这里习得的文字格外持久。
study:2.hook: The swaying herb pointed, without wind, toward the sealed west shelf.
study:2.line: 'Every hour of *study* here is worth three hours anywhere else on the mountain.'

mark:2.en: Xiaoxing handed me my first graded exercise — a sheet of rice paper covered in my clumsy attempts at the flight word. Beside each attempt, Master Qingwu had left a small *mark*: a circle, a dot, or a single brushstroke slash. The circles warmed my palm. The slashes felt like cool water. At the bottom was no mark at all — only an empty space the exact shape of a moth.
mark:2.cnHint: 师尊在我的练习纸上留下了各种____，最后却留下了空白。
mark:2.hook: The moth-shaped blank began, very slowly, to glow.
mark:2.line: 'Each *mark* here tells you not what you did, but what the word heard from you.'

choice:2.en: At the Gate of Paths, two scrolls lay open on the altar stone — one edged in silver, one in deep blue. Shen Wujiu stood back and said nothing. Master Qingwu had taught us that a disciple's first *choice* of word-path shaped every lesson that followed. My hand moved before my mind did, settling above the blue scroll. A single cloud drifted up from the sea of clouds below and stopped level with my eyes.
choice:2.cnHint: 面对两卷经文，我做出了入门后的第一个____，云海随之异动。
choice:2.hook: The silver scroll rolled itself shut the moment my hand moved.
choice:2.line: 'A *choice* made with the hand and the heart together is the kind the mountain remembers.'

part:2.en: The welcome ceremony was nearly over when Xiaoxing leaned close and whispered that I had missed one *part* — a small rite performed alone at midnight, at the edge of the outer cliff, where new disciples spoke their first chosen word into the open sky. No one had told me. 'It is never written down,' she said, with a careful smile. Above us, a single lantern broke free of its cord and drifted, unhurried, toward the cliff's edge.
part:2.cnHint: 小星悄悄告诉我，入门仪式还有一个____我尚未完成。
part:2.hook: The lantern stopped at the cliff's edge, as if waiting for me.
part:2.line: 'That *part* of the rite belongs to you alone — no master watches, and no one asks what word you chose.'

bank:2.en: Master Qingwu led us to the inner library, where every shelf curved like a river bend. 'This,' she said softly, 'is our *bank* of sacred words — ten thousand formulas gathered across three hundred years.' I ran my fingers along the spines of the scrolls, each one humming with quiet power. Outside, the wind shifted without warning.
bank:2.cnHint: 青雾师尊带我们来到内院藏书阁，那里珍藏着三百年来积累的词语____。
bank:2.hook: One scroll at the far end glowed with a cold, uninvited light.
bank:2.line: 'This *bank* of sacred words holds every healing formula the sect has ever known.'

statement:2.en: Shen Wujiu unrolled a scroll and read aloud a single *statement* carved into its first line: 'One who speaks a word in full sincerity calls the clouds to answer.' The hall fell silent. I repeated the words under my breath, and the floor stone beneath me trembled once, as though something deep below had heard.
statement:2.cnHint: 师兄大声念出卷首那句____，大厅随之陷入寂静。
statement:2.hook: A thin crack split the stone between my feet, shaped like an open mouth.
statement:2.line: 'Read this *statement* carefully — it is the first vow every disciple must speak aloud.'

identify:2.en: Master Qingwu placed five plain jars on the table and asked me to *identify* the one filled with the word for 'stillness.' I closed my eyes and listened. Four jars hummed like busy streams, but one held a silence so complete it seemed to breathe. I chose it. She did not smile — she only looked at the sky.
identify:2.cnHint: 青雾师尊让我从五个罐子中____出装有'静'字的那个。
identify:2.hook: Above us, a single cloud stopped moving and held its shape like a held breath.
identify:2.line: 'Can you *identify* which vessel holds the word for stillness, without opening any of them?'

comprehension:2.en: Xiaoxing passed me a practice scroll that tested *comprehension* of the five root formulas. I answered three with ease, but the fourth stopped me cold — its meaning hid behind a layer of old phrasing I had never seen. I stared at it so long the ink seemed to shift. A chill rose from the paper without reason.
comprehension:2.cnHint: 小星递给我一份测试五种根本口诀____的练习卷，第四题让我卡住了。
comprehension:2.hook: The ink on the fourth question slowly rearranged itself into a shape I did not recognise.
comprehension:2.line: 'Your *comprehension* of the root formulas is strong, but the fourth one is meant to resist you.'

require:2.en: The welcome rite was nearly over when Master Qingwu raised one hand. 'The final step will *require* each of you to leave one spoken word inside the gate stone,' she said. Shen Wujiu went first, pressing his lips close to the pale rock. When my turn came, the stone was already warmer than it should have been.
require:2.cnHint: 入门仪式尾声，师尊说最后一步____每人在门石中留下一个口述的字。
require:2.hook: The gate stone glowed faintly red where Shen Wujiu's word still lived inside it.
require:2.line: 'The rite will *require* your sincerest word — a hollow one will shatter the stone entirely.'

least:2.en: Xiaoxing showed me her collection of copied formulas, each page dense with careful writing. 'Learn the *least* powerful one first,' she urged, 'because even a small word, spoken wrong, can unravel stitching in the air around you.' I looked at the simplest formula on the page, and noticed it had already been copied a hundred times — each copy slightly different.
least:2.cnHint: 小星建议我先从____强大的那个口诀开始练习，因为即使小字念错也会有影响。
least:2.hook: The hundred copies of the simplest formula were all written in different hands.
least:2.line: 'Master the *least* powerful word first — even novice errors in it have left scars on this mountain.'

following:2.en: Shen Wujiu handed me a sealed note with the *following* instructions written inside: report to the Echo Terrace before the third bell, bring no scrolls, and speak to no one along the path. I folded it closed, already uneasy. When I looked up, the path to the terrace was empty — but someone had left fresh footprints in the pale dust.
following:2.cnHint: 师兄递给我一张便条，里面写着____的指示：天亮前去回音台，不带卷轴，沿途不得与人交谈。
following:2.hook: The footprints in the dust led to the terrace but did not lead back.
following:2.line: 'The *following* instructions come from Master Qingwu herself, so do not alter a single step.'

decide:2.en: At the fork between the Herb Path and the Word Tower, I had to *decide* which way to go before the morning bell rang. Xiaoxing had pointed left; Shen Wujiu had pointed right, saying nothing more. I stood still, and the wind pressed at my back from the left — steady, almost deliberate. I chose the Word Tower. The bell rang the moment my foot crossed the step.
decide:2.cnHint: 在草药小路与字塔的岔路口，我必须在晨钟敲响前____走哪条路。
decide:2.hook: The bell's echo lasted twice as long as it ever had before.
decide:2.line: 'You must *decide* your first path alone — the mountain reads the heart behind the choice.'
